formula:
Gold desk prediction ledger, scoring and learning. Numbers only from data/live.json and data/rates.json.
No AI is used anywhere here; every number is plain arithmetic or least squares, written to JSON.

Prices
  International gold in rupees (Rs/10 g, before duty) = COMEX gold (US$/oz) x USD/INR / 31.1035 x 10
  Landed cost (Rs/10 g, before GST)                   = international x (1 + customs duty%)          [market-value basis]
  Indian premium (+) / discount (-) %                  = IBJA 999 closing / landed cost - 1
     (COMEX reference = average of previous and same-day COMEX close, approximating the price at IBJA's afternoon rate)
Forecast of the % change of gold in rupees over h days (h = 7, 30):
  d% = w_mom * (gold-in-rupees % change over last h days)
     + w_real * (US 10-yr real yield change over last h days, percentage points)
     + w_usd * (US broad dollar index % change over last h days)
     + w_fx * (USD/INR % change over last h days)
  weights re-fitted every run by ridge least squares on realised history (heavy shrinkage toward 'no change');
  a variable keeps weight only if it cuts walk-forward error by at least 1%, and the model as a whole must beat 'no change'.
  The forecast is applied to the IBJA 999 closing rate; live predictions are scored on the IBJA closing rate.
lessons: 7-day back-test (2018-11-01 to 2026-11-12, 416 calls, gold in rupees): direction right 36.8% vs 36.8% for 'assume no change'; average error 1.898% vs 1.898%. Un-gated model (all four variables): 36.8% right, error 1.908%.
7-day: no variable has proven predictive value, so the model forecast is 'no change' and it is not used for the call. Gold behaves close to a random walk.

30-day back-test (2018-11-26 to 2026-10-19, 409 calls, gold in rupees): direction right 33.3% vs 33.3% for 'assume no change'; average error 3.935% vs 3.935%. Un-gated model (all four variables): 33.5% right, error 3.972%.
30-day: no variable has proven predictive value, so the model forecast is 'no change' and it is not used for the call. Gold behaves close to a random walk.

Rule 'buy on a 3.0% dip, wait after a 3.0% jump' (30-day outcome, since 2017-11-09): right 52.4% of 399 signals (wait: 40.9% of 254, opposite action 59.1%, buy now: 72.4% of 145, opposite action 27.6%).
Rule 'premium/discount above 2.0%': 19 signals in the IBJA history held, right 36.8% (buy now: 36.8% of 19).
Rule sides used for today's call: 'buy after a dip'. Not used: 'wait after a jump', 'buy when India is at a discount', 'wait when India is at a premium'.

Chart indicators (14 tested, 2016-11-24 to 2026-11-24): none cut 21-day error by 1% vs the drift and 'no change', so none feeds the call. Closest on direction: 50-day average above/below 200-day (golden/death cross state), right 56.4% vs 59.9% for 'always the usual direction'. Support levels held 72.8% of touches vs 75.1% for random levels; resistance 63.8% vs 59.1%.

technical.method:
Technical view: standard chart indicators on gold in rupees, each back-tested walk-forward before it may count.

Series: international gold in rupees before duty (Rs/10 g) = COMEX close x USD/INR (ECB) / 31.1035 x 10; daily highs and
lows the same way from COMEX highs/lows (for ATR, Donchian and swing levels). About 10 years of daily data (2016 on).
No look-ahead: every reading on day t uses data up to t only; a swing high/low becomes a level only K days after it.
Each indicator gives +1 (points up), -1 (points down) or 0 (no signal).
Scores, for horizons of 5, 10 and 21 trading days:
  hit rate      = share of signal days where the price moved the way the signal pointed; compared with
                  'always assume the usual direction' (the drift) on the same days
  error         = forecast a + b*signal, re-fitted every 21 trading days on outcomes already known; compared with
                  'no change' (0) and with the drift alone (a)
  decision value= a buyer who must hold gold by day N: signal up -> buy now (pays carrying cost), down -> buy on day N,
                  none -> half and half; average cost compared with buying immediately and with buying on day N
Gate (same rule as the model): an indicator may feed the main call only if, at 21 trading days (about 30 calendar days,
the call's window), it cuts walk-forward error by at least 1% versus the drift alone AND versus 'no change'.
Numbers only from data/live.json; plain arithmetic, no AI.

ibja.note: IBJA-equivalent level = world-price level x (IBJA rate / world price in rupees on the IBJA date); the ratio carries duty and the local premium
